glance_notes.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The deadline to register for Arkansas's November 3, 2026 General Election is Monday, October 5, 2026. The statutory 30-day date falls on Sunday, October 4, so Arkansas's deadline-extension rule moves the deadline to the following business day.

glance_notes.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Early Voting: Early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins Monday, October 19, 2026, and ends at 5:00 p.m. Monday, November 2, 2026.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Arkansas uses a paper voter registration application. You can obtain the application from your county clerk, the Arkansas Secretary of State, a local revenue or DMV office, public library, disability agency, or military recruitment office. The Secretary of State also provides a printable application and an online form for requesting that an application be mailed to you. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be an Arkansas resident, be age 18 or turn 18 on or before the next election, not be a convicted felon whose sentence has not been discharged or pardoned, and not be presently adjudged mentally incompetent as to your ability to vote by a court of competent jurisdiction.
register.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Voter Registration Information
register.internal_note: The official registration page directly establishes that Arkansas requires a paper Voter Registration Application, lists official places to obtain it, and states the registration qualifications. Registration identification is separate from identification required when voting.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Arkansas VoterView to check whether your voter registration has been processed. The Secretary of State advises voters not to assume registration is complete simply because an application was submitted; your county clerk processes the application and sends an acknowledgment. VoterView can also be used to check your registration information.
check_registration.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Arkansas Secretary of State Voter Registration Information — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/) — states that registration is processed by the county clerk and directs voters to VoterView to check status.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For a new registration, Arkansas requires the application to be submitted to an official voter registration agency or mailed no later than 30 days before the election. A mailed application's postmark is treated as its submission date. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the normal 30-day date is Sunday, October 4, so the official 2026 election calendar sets the actual registration deadline as Monday, October 5, 2026. A voter moving from one Arkansas county to another has a separate rule: the updated registration must be received by the county clerk in the new county no later than four days before a scheduled election.
deadlines.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The 2026 Election Calendar identifies October 4 as 30 days before the General Election and expressly moves the actual deadline to Monday, October 5 under Ark. Code § 7-1-108. Additional verification source: Arkansas Secretary of State FAQ — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/frequently-asked-questions/65](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/frequently-asked-questions/65) — supports the general 30-day rule, mail postmark rule, and separate four-day deadline for an interstate-county address change.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Arkansas VoterView to find your assigned polling location. Your precinct is based on where you live, and your polling site is assigned by your county election commission.
polling_place.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Arkansas Secretary of State Voting in Arkansas — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/voting-in-arkansas](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/voting-in-arkansas) — states that the precinct is determined by residence, the polling site is assigned by the county election commission, and VoterView provides polling-site information.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Registered Arkansas voters may vote at their assigned polling site on Election Day. Check VoterView before leaving for the polls to confirm your registration and polling location. Arkansas also requires voters voting in person to verify their registration with qualifying photo identification or applicable documentation; voters unable to satisfy the identification requirement at the polling site may cast a provisional ballot.
election_day.glance_value: Vote at your assigned polling site
election_day.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Voting in Arkansas
election_day.internal_note: Supplemental verification source for identification and provisional voting: Arkansas Secretary of State Voter Registration Information — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/).

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Arkansas polling places are open from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. The official 2026 election calendar confirms these hours for the November 3, 2026 General Election.
polling_hours.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: The 2026 calendar specifically states that polls for the November 3 General Election are open 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., citing Ark. Code §§ 7-5-102 and 7-5-304(a). The Secretary of State Voting in Arkansas page independently states the same Election Day hours.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Arkansas provides in-person early voting. For preferential primary and general elections, early voting begins 15 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins October 19. Standard hours are 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Monday through Friday and 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Saturday, with early voting ending at 5:00 p.m. on Monday, November 2. Off-site early-voting hours may vary by county, so check with your county clerk for local locations and schedules.
early_voting.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
early_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar establishes the October 19 start, weekday/Saturday hours, and November 2 5:00 p.m. ending time. Additional verification source: Arkansas Secretary of State Voting in Arkansas — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/voting-in-arkansas](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/voter-information/voter-registration-information/voting-in-arkansas) — explains that most counties use the county clerk's office and that off-site hours may vary.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Arkansas absentee voting is available to voters who will be unavoidably absent from their polling site on Election Day, cannot attend because of illness or physical disability, qualify as certain uniformed-service or merchant-marine voters or their eligible family members away because of active duty, or are Arkansas-resident U.S. citizens temporarily outside the United States. Request an absentee-ballot application from your county clerk or download the state application and return it to the clerk where you are registered. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, applications sent by mail, fax, or email must be received by October 27. In-person applications from the voter, a designated bearer, or administrator are due by the close of regular business October 30; an authorized agent for a medically unable voter has until 1:30 p.m. Election Day. Non-UOCAVA ballots returned by mail must reach the county clerk by 7:30 p.m. Election Day. Different delivery rules apply to ballots personally returned by voters, designated bearers, administrators, authorized agents, and UOCAVA voters.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Excuse required; deadlines depend on delivery method
absentee_mail.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State absentee page establishes eligibility and method-specific application and ballot-return deadlines. Additional verification source: 2026 Election Calendar — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/2026_Election_Calendar_Rev._6-2025_.pdf](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/2026_Election_Calendar_Rev._6-2025_.pdf) — confirms October 27 for mail/fax/email applications, October 30 for in-person applications and specified personal ballot returns, 1:30 p.m. Election Day for authorized-agent applications, and 7:30 p.m. Election Day for ordinary mailed ballots and authorized-agent returns. UOCAVA voters have separate rules addressed in the military_overseas section.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: When voting in person, Arkansas voters generally must present a document or identification card showing the voter's name and photograph and issued by the United States, the State of Arkansas, or an accredited postsecondary educational institution in Arkansas. If the document has an expiration date, it may be current or expired no more than four years before the election. Examples include a driver's license, photo identification card, concealed-handgun carry license, U.S. passport, qualifying postsecondary-school employee badge or ID, U.S. military ID, qualifying public-assistance photo ID, or Arkansas voter verification card. Residents of state-licensed long-term-care or residential-care facilities may instead provide documentation from the facility administrator confirming residence. A voter unable to provide the required verification when voting in person may cast a provisional ballot and has a post-election process for supplying qualifying identification. Voters without qualifying identification may obtain a free voter verification card from their county clerk.
voter_id.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Voter Verification FAQ
voter_id.internal_note: Official FAQ directly supports the identification characteristics, examples, long-term-care exception, provisional-ballot remedy, noon-on-the-Monday-after-election identification deadline, and free voter verification card. This section concerns identification when voting and intentionally does not conflate those rules with identification information requested on a mailed registration application.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Arkansas law provides voting access and assistance for voters with disabilities. Polling locations must provide reasonable and adequate accessible methods so a voter with a disability can personally and secretly cast a ballot. A voter who needs assistance may use accessible voting equipment or ask for assistance. A voter who, because of a physical, sensory, or other disability, tells a poll worker that they cannot stand in line for an extended period is entitled to assistance advancing to the front of the line.
accessible_voting.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — State of Arkansas Voter Rights
accessible_voting.internal_note: The official voter-rights publication directly describes accessible polling locations, accessible voting equipment, voter assistance, and the line-access accommodation, citing Ark. Code §§ 7-5-310 and 7-5-311. These statutory provisions are also contained in the Secretary of State's 2025 Arkansas Election Laws and Constitution compilation: [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/Arkansas_Election_Laws_and_Constitution_2025_Edition.pdf](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/Arkansas_Election_Laws_and_Constitution_2025_Edition.pdf).

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Arkansas provides special absentee-voting procedures for voters covered by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act. Eligible voters include qualifying active-duty uniformed-service members and their spouses and dependents who are absent because of that service, qualifying Merchant Marine members and their spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens residing or temporarily outside the United States. These voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as an emergency backup if the regular ballot does not arrive. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, a qualifying UOCAVA ballot must be voted by Election Day and received by the county clerk by 5:00 p.m. ten calendar days after the election.
military_overseas.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Citizens
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State UOCAVA page defines covered voters and provides FPCA/FWAB information. Additional verification source: Arkansas Secretary of State 2026 Election Calendar — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/2026_Election_Calendar_Rev._6-2025_.pdf](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/2026_Election_Calendar_Rev._6-2025_.pdf) — confirms that qualified overseas electors and active-duty uniformed personnel must sign/date and timely mail their ballot by Election Day and that it must be received by 5:00 p.m. ten calendar days after the election.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: Arkansas students may retain residence for voting purposes at the place where they lived before becoming a student, or a student may establish residence at the new location if the student intends it to be their residence. A student may not be registered and vote in more than one place. Students registering at a college location must otherwise follow Arkansas's normal voter-registration rules and deadlines.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may establish residence at school
student_voting.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Voter Registration FAQ
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State FAQ expressly addresses college students and states that they may retain their prior residence or intend the new place to be their residence, but cannot register and vote in more than one place. The related voter-registration FAQ identifies Ark. Code § 7-5-201.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Arkansas voters can use VoterView to see the sample ballot associated with their registration and voting location when ballots are available. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, county election commissions must upload sample ballots to VoterView by October 14, 2026.
sample_ballot.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Arkansas Secretary of State For Voters — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/for-voters](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/elections/for-voters) — identifies VoterView as the official tool for registration status, polling locations, and sample ballots. The 2026 Election Calendar — [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/2026_Election_Calendar_Rev._6-2025_.pdf](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/2026_Election_Calendar_Rev._6-2025_.pdf) — sets October 14, 2026 as the deadline for county boards of election commissioners to upload General Election sample ballots to VoterView under Ark. Code § 7-5-206(b)(2)(A).

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Arkansas Secretary of State, Elections Division, State Capitol, Room 026, 500 Woodlane Street, Little Rock, AR 72201. Phone: 501-682-5070. Toll-free outside the Little Rock area: 800-482-1127. Email: electionsemail@sos.arkansas.gov. County clerks handle voter registration and many local voting and absentee-ballot services.
contact.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The Secretary of State contact page directly verifies the Elections Division phone, toll-free number, and email. Elections Division location as Room 026 at the State Capitol is independently confirmed by the Secretary of State Duties of the Office page and the current 2025-2026 Initiative and Referendum Handbook. County-clerk role is documented throughout the official voter-registration and absentee-voting pages.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Arkansas Secretary of State Elections website for statewide election information and VoterView for registration status, polling locations, and sample ballots. For registration records, absentee voting, and other county-administered election services, contact your county clerk. The Secretary of State maintains an official directory of Arkansas county clerks.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, VoterView & county clerks
official_resources.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State — For Voters
official_resources.internal_note: Official direct-action VoterView: [https://www.voterview.ar-nova.org/VoterView](https://www.voterview.ar-nova.org/VoterView) — registration status, polling locations, and sample ballots. Official county-clerk directory: [https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/ARCountyClerks.pdf](https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/elections/ARCountyClerks.pdf) — local clerk contact information. Arkansas Secretary of State More Election Information page also links VoterView, the absentee application, county-clerk contacts, FPCA, FWAB, and FVAP resources.
